hypothesis: This is the test arm of the width-scaling test. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=256, best-of-3 controls, seed 22, 6000 steps. Prediction: the N=128 force deficit is at least partly a capacity bottleneck. The d_model=64 to d_model=128 gap fell from 0.143 to 0.108 because N=128 force rose from 0.681 to 0.718 while N=64 stayed near 0.82-0.83. Doubling width again raises N=128 trained force R2 further, to >= 0.74 at the best-margin layer (probes_final, unrounded, layer reported), and shrinks the same-seed N=64 minus N=128 gap against the paired d_model=256 N=64 arm to <= 0.085, at least 0.02 below the d_model=128 gap. accel_step stays flat. A layer-1 same-layer gap is also reported wherever both arms list layer 1. Cross-layer pairs are flagged. Both arms' run IDs are cited. If the paired arm is unavailable, the gap is reported as not computed. All comparisons use trained R2.
expected_if_true: N=128 final force R2 >= 0.74. Best-layer gap to the paired d256 N=64 arm <= 0.085, and the layer-1 same-layer gap (if available) <= 0.10. accel_step headroom-normalised margin in [0.60, 0.90], within 0.05 of the d128 N=128 seed-22 value (0.868).
expected_if_false: N=128 final force R2 <= 0.73 and the best-layer gap to the paired d256 N=64 arm >= 0.10. That would mean the d128 shrinkage did not continue, and the deficit is a width-independent steps_per_orbit offset of about 0.10 for this seed. A gap in (0.085, 0.10) is inconclusive.
